unit: odds ratio of contacting a GP for a mental-health problem in the past 12 months per 1-percentage-point rise in the national unemployment rate (change variable), working-age MEN; y-standardised
definition: Eurobarometer 2002, 2005/06, 2010, 27 EU countries, 22,978 men and 28,014 women aged 20-65; three-level logistic model; Model 1 (1.031) and Model 4 controlling for MHI-5 mental health (1.021), both p<.05. Women: 1.031 (Model 1) to 1.010 (Model 4), not significant.

source.authors: Buffel V, van de Straat V, Bracke P
source.title: Employment status and mental health care use in times of economic contraction: a repeated cross-sectional study in Europe, using a three-level model
source.publisher_or_journal: International Journal for Equity in Health 14:29
source.locator: Table 5 'General practitioner consultations regressed on employment status...', row 'Change in unemployment', Men Models 1-5; Women Models 1-5

derivation: As an elasticity of GP mental-health contacts to the unemployment RATE (ours): at a baseline unemployment rate of about 9%, a 1pp rise is an 11% relative rise; odds up 2.1-3.1% (odds approximate probability for a rare outcome) gives an elasticity of about 0.19 to 0.28 for men and about 0.09 to 0.28 (n.s.) for women.
quality_note: The only EU27 multi-country estimate found of how care use for mental health moves with unemployment; y-standardised ORs are not raw ORs; contact is self-reported; the effect for men holds after controlling for mental health (medicalisation).

source.locator: Section 3 Results and Table 2; cost GBP 55 in Section 2.5; 'estimated to be £91 per person'

unit: percent increase in SNAP enrolment per 1 percentage point rise in the unemployment rate (semi-elasticity); value = contemporaneous state-level, value_high = cumulative 3-year county population-weighted
definition: US state/county panels 1990s-2011 with state and year fixed effects: a one percentage point increase in the state unemployment rate raises SNAP enrolment by six percent (also Mabli & Ferrerosa 2010). County model with two lags: persistent 1 pp rise gives 11% cumulative increase after three years (county-equal weights), 20% population-weighted. Local unemployment explains at least two-thirds of the 2007-2011 enrolment rise.

source.title: The Decline, Rebound, and Further Rise in SNAP Enrollment: Disentangling Business Cycle Fluctuations and Policy Changes
source.locator: p.22-23 (Section on unemployment, eq. 7-8, Figure 7, Table 3): 'raises SNAP enrollment by six percent'; 'increase in SNAP enrollment reaching 11% after three years'; '20% cumulative increase'

derivation: Converted to the tool's proportional elasticity only for illustration: at a 5% base unemployment rate a 1 pp rise is +20% in unemployment, so +6% enrolment = elasticity 0.3 (contemporaneous) and +11% to +20% = 0.55 to 1.0 (3-year cumulative). Depends on the base unemployment rate.
quality_note: Authors stress these are historical associations, not causal (footnote 35: caseworker ratios and policy may respond to unemployment). US food-assistance programme with high take-up responsiveness; EU minimum income schemes have stricter asset tests.

unit: percentage point change in the probability of leaving the regional minimum income programme (RMI) per 1 percent increase in the provincial unemployment rate (marginal effect, discrete hazard)

All periods: -0.60 pp; 2005-08 expansion: +0.21 pp; 2009-13 recession: -0.75 pp; 2014-16 aftermath: -2.11 pp. Higher unemployment lengthens spells, i.e. raises caseload through lower outflow.

source.title: Differential Effects of Expansions and Recessions on Social Assistance Duration: The Case of Regional Minimum Income Programmes in Spain
source.publisher_or_journal: Hacienda Publica Espanola / Review of Public Economics 248(1/2024):115-141
source.locator: p.126 text and Table 3 (unemployment -0.0060***); p.130 Table 4 by period (0.0021, -0.0075, -0.0211)

quality_note: Large administrative panel; association between provincial unemployment and exit hazards, not a caseload elasticity directly; inflow response not estimated here. 'Per 1 percent' in text likely means per percentage point.

definition: Adults in Great Britain Wealth and Assets Survey; being in arrears = 2+ consecutive missed repayments on any credit/household bill, or card arrears; controls for ln(non-arrear debt), income etc.; individual, year and region-year FE. unit: percentage-point rise in household food insecurity prevalence per 1 percentage-point rise in unemployment rate (first-difference, cross-national)
definition: 21 EU countries 2004-2012, Eurostat EU-SILC food insecurity = inability to afford a meal with meat/chicken/fish (or vegetarian equivalent) every second day; cross-national first-difference models. Same model: each USD 1000 fall in annual average wages +0.62pp (0.27 to 0.97); each USD 1000 per capita of social protection spending reduced the unemployment association by 0.05pp (-0.10 to -0.0007); effects insignificant above USD 10,000 per capita social protection.

source.title: Food insecurity and social protection in Europe: Quasi-natural experiment of Europe’s great recessions 2004-2012
source.locator: Abstract (95% CI in brackets)

Measures food INSECURITY prevalence (EU-SILC deprivation item), not food-bank DEMAND; a semi-elasticity in pp, not a % elasticity. Converting to a % elasticity needs national base rates of food insecurity and unemployment (not done here). EU-wide pooled; country-specific slopes not in abstract.

unit: percentage-point change in food bank use per capita (Trussell parcels per 100 population) per 1 percentage-point higher unemployment rate
definition: Linear regression of Trussell Trust food parcel distribution 2010-13 in 251 UK local authorities with operating food banks (575 LA-years), SEs clustered by LA, adjusting for number of food banks per 100,000 and years of operation, sanctions, welfare spending cuts, GVA, Christian share. Same table: each 1pp higher adverse sanction rate +0.09pp (0.01-0.17); each 1pp cut in central welfare spending +0.16pp (0.10-0.22); each additional food bank per 100,000 +0.66pp; each additional year of operation +0.38pp. Parcel distribution rose from about 0.6 to 2.2 per 100 population 2010-2013. Table 1 (346 LAs): each 1pp higher unemployment raised odds of a first food bank opening next year OR 1.08 (1.02-1.14).

source.authors: Loopstra R, Reeves A, Taylor-Robinson D, Barr B, McKee M, Stuckler D
source.title: Austerity, sanctions, and the rise of food banks in the UK
source.locator: p.5 Table 2 row ’Each one percentage point higher unemployment rate’; p.2 text (0.6 to 2.2 per 100); p.4 Table 1
